title: Jharkhand, which is known for its pristine forests and natural resources, was created on November 15, 2000, from what was previously the southern areas of Bihar
author: PTI
content_html:
President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (November 15, 2026) greeted the residents of Jharkhand on the State's foundation day and noted that the State is a unique confluence of tribal pride, cultural diversity, and natural wealth.

Jharkhand, which is known for its pristine forests and natural resources, was created on November 15, 2000, from what was previously the southern areas of Bihar.

"Heartfelt greetings to all brothers and sisters of Jharkhand on the State Foundation Day! Our state is a unique confluence of tribal pride, cultural diversity, and natural wealth," Mr. Modi said in a post X in Hindi.

The Prime Minister said the State's dense forests, scenic waterfalls, and historical sites enrich its distinct identity.

"The traditions here have continuously drawn inspiration from the tales of valour and sacrifice of Bhagwan Birsa Munda Ji," he said.

Mr. Modi said that from minerals and energy to handicrafts and tourism, this State holds immense possibilities.

The Prime Minister said he was confident that on the strength of the resolve and capability of the hardworking and talented residents of Jharkhand, the state will scale new heights of development.

"My wish is that this special occasion brings happiness, prosperity, and well-being into the lives of all the people here," he said.

President Droupadi Murmu extends greetings

President Droupadi Murmu extended greetings on Jharkhand’s foundation day and wished its hardworking, talented residents success in taking the State to new heights of development and prosperity.

“This land, home to divine figures such as Dharti Aba Bhagwan Birsa Munda and great heroes such as Sidho-Kanhu, has a distinctive identity rooted in its rich tribal culture, vibrant folk traditions and natural and mineral wealth,” she said in a post on X in Hindi.

“I hope that Jharkhand’s hardworking and talented residents, cherishing their rich heritage, will take the state to new heights of development and prosperity,” the President said.

Jharkhand was formed on this day in 2000 after being carved out of Bihar.

“On the occasion of Jharkhand State Foundation Day, my heartfelt best wishes to all the residents of the State,” she said.

In a separate post, the President extended greetings on the birth anniversary of legendary freedom fighter and tribal rights leader Birsa Munda.

“On the sacred occasion of the birth anniversary of Dharti Aba, Bhagwan Birsa Munda, I extend my heartfelt greetings to all fellow citizens on ‘Janjatiya Gaurav Divas’,” she said in the post.

The tribal icon’s birth anniversary is celebrated as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.

“This day is an opportunity to remember our rich tribal heritage and the historic contributions of tribal communities to the nation. I hope that all fellow citizens will preserve our invaluable heritage while moving forward on the path of inclusive development,” the President said.

title: PM Modi pays tribute to Birsa Munda on birth anniversary
author: PTI
content_html:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (November 15, 2026) paid tributes to tribal icon Birsa Munda on his 151st birth anniversary and extended greetings on the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas.

In a post in Hindi on X, the Prime Minister said the courage, struggle and sacrifice of 'Dharti Aaba' would continue to inspire generations to uphold self-respect, freedom and rights.

भगवान बिरसा मुंडा जी की जयंती पर उन्हें समस्त देशवासियों की ओर से मेरा कोटि-कोटि नमन।  आप सभी को इस दिव्य अवसर से जुड़े जनजातीय गौरव दिवस की बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं। धरती आबा का अदम्य साहस, संघर्ष और बलिदान देश की हर पीढ़ी को स्वाभिमान, स्वतंत्रता और अधिकारों की रक्षा के लिए प्रेरित करता रहेगा।  उनसे प्रेरणा लेकर हमारी सरकार जनजातीय भाई-बहनों के सम्मान, अवसर और समृद्धि के लिए कोई कोर-कसर नहीं छोड़ रही है।  आइए, सभी मिलकर राष्ट्र निर्माण में जनजातीय समाज के बहुमूल्य योगदान को नमन करें।

— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 15, 2026

He said the government, drawing inspiration from Birsa Munda, was committed to ensuring dignity, opportunities and prosperity for the tribal community.

Mr. Modi also called upon people to recognise and honour the invaluable contribution of tribal communities to nation-building.

PM @narendramodi pays floral tribute to Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda at parliament complex in Delhi https://t.co/1aQMnVQJEA

— Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (@MIB_India) November 15, 2026

Since 2021, Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas is observed every year on November 15 to commemorate the birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda.

title: Prince William, Princess Kate to visit Mumbai for Earthshot Prize Awards; gully cricket, Metro ride, Bollywood on itinerary
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Prince William and Catherine, the Princess of Wales, will visit Mumbai from November 16 to 18 for the sixth annual Earthshot Prize Summit and Awards Night, with a three-day itinerary featuring engagements focused on environmental sustainability, gully cricket, public transport and India’s film industry.

The visit will mark the royal couple’s second official trip to India. According to a statement issued ahead of the visit, the Prince and Princess will participate in several engagements across Mumbai aimed at highlighting innovation, youth leadership and cultural ties between India and the United Kingdom.

Also read: Royal couple take guard, Mumbai bowled out

The couple will begin their engagements on Monday (November 16, 2026), with an event celebrating Mumbai’s tradition of gully cricket and the shared passion for the sport in India and the U.K.

Later in the day, Prince William will travel on the Mumbai Metro to highlight the importance of sustainable urban transport. He will also attend the Earthshot Prize Impact Assembly, where discussions will focus on scaling solutions to major environmental challenges.

On Tuesday (November 17, 2026), the Prince will meet the 2026 Earthshot Prize finalists before joining Princess Kate for the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards Ceremony at the Museum of Solutions.

The children’s awards follow a nationwide programme involving 15,000 schools across 24 Indian states, which invited children aged nine to 17 to develop solutions to environmental problems affecting their communities.

The couple will attend the Earthshot Prize Awards Night later that evening. The annual environmental initiative recognises five winners working on solutions to challenges including climate change, air pollution, waste management, ocean conservation and biodiversity loss. Each winner receives £1 million to support their work.

India has produced more Earthshot Prize winners and finalists than any other country, according to the statement.

On Wednesday (November 18, 2026), the couple will visit an institution dedicated to traditional craftsmanship to learn how preserving craft techniques can contribute to sustainable textile production.

Princess Kate will also visit a maternity hospital in Mumbai, where she will interact with healthcare professionals and families to understand approaches to maternal healthcare and support during the earliest stages of family life.

The royal couple will conclude their visit at Dharma Productions, where they will learn about India’s film industry and its global cultural influence. The engagement will also highlight the longstanding creative connections between India and the United Kingdom.

Princess Kate’s attendance at the Earthshot Prize Awards Night will be her first since the ceremony was held in Boston in 2022.

title: Shooter wanted in murder of influencer Mad Sandhu among 2 arrested, were planning attack on Amitabh Bachchan
author: Lavpreet Kaur
content_html:
The Delhi Police Special Cell has foiled a suspected firing plot targeting Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan outside his Mumbai residence, with the arrest of a shooter involved in the murder of Instagram influencer Mad Sandhu in Amritsar last month, officials said.

The investigation into the arrests of two shooters linked to a foreign-based gangster has revealed that Deepak Singh alias Deep was instructed to remain in Mumbai for an extended period to execute the attack on the actor, allegedly over his purported remarks on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, police sources said.

Mr. Bachchan has consistently denied ever making any inciting remarks during the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

The two accused, identified as Vikas Thakur alias Vicky (25), a resident of Jalandhar, and Deepak Singh, a resident of Tarn Taran in Punjab, were arrested in separate intelligence-led operations in Delhi and Mumbai. Their arrests also helped avert a planned extortion-driven shooting targeting a Delhi-based businessman, the police said.

According to the police, Vikas had travelled from Mumbai to Delhi on the instructions of the foreign-based gangster to carry out the shooting at the businessman. Deep was supposed to join him later. However, the Special Cell intercepted Vikas before the planned attack could be executed.

Following his arrest, the police used intelligence inputs to track down Deep in Mumbai, where he was hiding after the October 3 murder of Mad Sandhu in Amritsar, Punjab. Deep is accused of carrying out the attack along with an associate, Palwinder alias Kaka, who has already been arrested by the Punjab Police.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (Special Cell) Narra Chaitanya said the arrests had helped thwart two planned attacks and an extortion-related shooting. The police also said the timely intervention prevented an attack on the Bollywood actor.

Criminal network

The police said Vikas had been working for different organised crime syndicates and had been tasked with arranging firearms, recruiting members and conducting reconnaissance of potential extortion targets.

Born into a lower-income family, Vikas was academically sound during his early school years but allegedly fell into bad company in the absence of parental supervision. He first came to police notice as a juvenile in 2019 in a snatching case and subsequently became involved in illegal betting and gambling.

In 2023, he began supplying illegal firearms to gangster Anmol Bishnoi. Following Bishnoi’s arrest, he shifted allegiance to gangsters Anil Pandit and Randeep Malik, undertaking various assignments, including arranging weapons, recruiting associates and conducting reconnaissance, the police said.

He later began operating independently, taking up assignments from different gangs in return for money. He subsequently came in contact with the foreign-based gangster who tasked him with carrying out the firing on the Bollywood actor in Mumbai.

Deep, meanwhile, had earlier worked as a commercial truck helper and driver. He was introduced to the foreign-based gangster through a local gang member and subsequently became involved in organised crime.

The police said Deep and his associate Palwinder targeted Mad Sandhu in Amritsar on October 3 on the gangster’s instructions. While Palwinder was arrested by the Punjab Police, Deep fled and took shelter in Mumbai.

The gangster subsequently instructed Deep to prolong his stay in Mumbai so that he could execute the planned firing on the actor. Vikas was also allegedly assigned the task of attacking the actor before being given the separate assignment targeting the Delhi businessman.

A case under the Arms Act has been registered at the Special Cell police station (FIR No. 261/2026 dated November 3). Further investigation is under way.

title: China border has become 'more alive,' India enhancing frontier infrastructure: Jaishankar
author: PTI
content_html:
India's border with China has become "more alive" and requires a much greater commitment of Indian troops on a sustained basis, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) as he listed New Delhi's policy approach to enhance infrastructure along the frontier.

Mr. Jaishankar also said that India has bolstered its military capabilities along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) since the deadly clashes in Eastern Ladakh's Galwan Valley in 2020.

His remarks at an interactive session at the HT Leadership Summit came amid ongoing efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to normalise their relations that came under severe strain following the over four-year border face-off in Eastern Ladakh.

"Just think about the last few years. How often do you now read - a new tunnel has been built, some new bridge has been built, another airfield has been commissioned. You're getting this news with greater and greater frequency," he said.

"What has happened today is the border with China has become more alive in a way. It has required a much greater commitment of troops on a sustained basis."

"The fact is that the work we had already done allowed that kind of numbers to be deployed out there, and the work we continue to do will maintain those numbers," he said.

After over four years of frosty ties over the eastern Ladakh military standoff, India and China began to repair relations following a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping in the Russian city of Kazan in October 2024 that took place after the face-off ended.

The talks between Mr. Modi and Mr. Xi covered a range of issues, including reducing their trade deficit, tackling challenges like terrorism and ensuring fair trade in multilateral platforms.

"I would say when it comes to the border, I would honestly make this point, and I think there's a lot of data and evidence to back it up, which is that the border infrastructure was really neglected till about a decade ago. I mean, people spoke about it, people drew up plan," Mr. Jaishankar said.

"If you actually go on the ground and see year-by-year how many kilometres of roads, what was the tunnelling, what was the positioning, I think anybody, and certainly anybody associated with the armed forces dealing with that sector knows the truth," he noted.

Mr. Jaishankar added: "It's really been in the last decade that that kind of attention, resources, policy push has been given."

The External Affairs Minister said India's capability to "deploy" its troops on that border has seen "a very marked" improvement.

Mr. Jaishankar also responded to a question on views about economic asymmetry between the two countries.

"On the economic side, the 1960s, 1970s, 1980s, this was the time the world was industrialising, developing countries were industrialising. Remember, when around the time when Rajiv Gandhi went to China in 1988, the Indian and Chinese economies were about the same size," he said.

"But the fact was that China, in the 1980s particularly, made a huge push towards modernisation and industrialisation. I'm sorry to say India in the 1980s simply missed the bus. Now in the 1990s, we did some corrections, reforms, but we did not carry through the reforms sector by sector and keep building and raising it," he said.

"I don't want you to think of it as a political point." The External Affairs Minister listed efforts by the Modi government in the areas of manufacturing and industrialisation.

"The fact is, there were decades where we missed out; now we have to play catch up; you can't play catch up by following the same track. You have to do leap-frogging. We'll have to build up our particular strengths to deal with this asymmetry issue."

"In asymmetry, you don't go toe-to-toe on every issue. You pick the issues where you feel you have the ability to make a big change. That's really what we think we're doing right now," he said.

title: Bar Council of A.P. appeals to Centre not to proceed with Evening Courts proposal
author: V. Raghavendra
content_html:
The Bar Council of Andhra Pradesh (BCAP) requested the Government of India not to proceed with the proposed establishment of Evening Courts and to take pro-active steps to achieve the stated objective, which is to reduce the huge load of cases pending disposal.

BCAP Secretary B. Padma Latha stated in a press release that the Centre should fill up all the posts of Presiding Officers in time as the vacancies were hampering the effective functioning of courts, provide sufficient infrastructure in the existing courts including the appointment of sufficient Staff, and increase the number of fast track courts.

She observed that the establishment of Evening Courts itself would not serve the purpose, rather cause inconvenience not only to the advocates but also to the litigant public. Besides, it would cause inconvenience to litigant public, especially for women to attend courts in evenings and travel back in the night.

It may be noted that the Central government proposed to set up Evening Courts in Andhra Pradesh, Bihar and Delhi in coordination with the respective High Courts on a pilot basis, for which retired judges were planned to be engaged.

Under the arrangement, courts operating during the standard daytime hours, will extend their sittings into the evening to hear and clear pending matters. This is meant to reduce the massive backlog of cases pending in courts.

title: 3 militants arrested for extortion in Manipur
author: PTI
content_html:
Security forces arrested three militants from different outfits in Manipur's Bishnupur and Imphal East districts for their alleged involvement in extortion, police said on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

Ngangom Ibomcha Singh (28), an active member of the banned Kangleipak Communist Party (Apunba), was apprehended on Thursday (November 12) for his alleged involvement in extortion from Irengbam Mamang Makha Leikai in Bishnupur district, an official said.

Further investigation led to the arrest of Konjengbam Kumarjit Singh (41), another active cadre of the outfit, from his residence in Nambol in the district the same day, he said.

On Friday (November 13), Thingbaijam Naobi Singh (47), a cadre of the United National Liberation Front (Pambei), was arrested on Wangkhei Ayangpalli Road in Imphal East district based on intelligence input. According to police, he was allegedly involved in extorting money from government offices and private firms.

UNLF (Pambei) signed a peace pact with the Centre and state government in 2023. However, its members allegedly continue with illegal activities, including extortion and arms possession, leading to their arrests.
